blocks.en: 📖 Deacon Family Ministry Plan — Unit 10: Sustaining the Plan — Challenges and Evaluation
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Plan de Ministerio Familiar del Diácono — Unidad 10: Sosteniendo el Plan — Desafíos y Evaluación

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Therefore, my beloved brethren, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord." — 1 Corinthians 15:58 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: «Así que, hermanos míos amados, estad firmes y constantes, creciendo en la obra del Señor siempre, sabiendo que vuestro trabajo en el Señor no es en vano.» — 1 Corintios 15:58 (RVG)

blocks.en: We have come a long way. We began with the biblical foundations of the diaconate and the character a deacon must have; we saw the vision and definition of the Deacon Family Ministry Plan, and how a church organizes it; and we followed the deacon through his ongoing care, his ministry of discipleship and evangelism, his work in times of crisis, and the meetings and the partnership with the pastor that support him. Now, in this final unit, we come to the last and most practical question of all: how is such a Plan to be sustained? For it is one thing to begin a good work, and quite another to keep it alive through the years.
blocks.es_reference: Hemos recorrido un largo camino. Comenzamos con los fundamentos bíblicos del diaconado y el carácter que un diácono debe tener; vimos la visión y la definición del Plan de Ministerio Familiar del Diácono, y cómo una iglesia lo organiza; y seguimos al diácono a través de su cuidado continuo, su ministerio de discipulado y evangelismo, su obra en tiempos de crisis, y las reuniones y la sociedad con el pastor que lo sostienen. Ahora, en esta unidad final, llegamos a la última y más práctica pregunta de todas: ¿cómo se ha de sostener tal Plan? Porque una cosa es comenzar una buena obra, y otra muy distinta mantenerla viva a través de los años.

blocks.en: Subject: sustaining the Deacon Family Ministry Plan through the years — its challenges and its evaluation.
blocks.es_reference: Tema: sostener el Plan de Ministerio Familiar del Diácono a través de los años — sus desafíos y su evaluación.

blocks.en: Proposition: The Plan endures only when a church honestly faces the challenges that erode it, takes deliberate steps to sustain it, evaluates it faithfully, and presses on in the assurance that such labor is never in vain.
blocks.es_reference: Proposición: El Plan perdura solo cuando una iglesia enfrenta honestamente los desafíos que lo erosionan, toma pasos deliberados para sostenerlo, lo evalúa fielmente, y sigue adelante en la certeza de que tal labor nunca es en vano.

blocks.en: We will look at why good plans fade, the challenges that threaten this one, how to sustain it, how to evaluate and renew it, and the reward that makes the whole labor worthwhile.
blocks.es_reference: Veremos por qué se desvanecen los buenos planes, los desafíos que amenazan a este, cómo sostenerlo, cómo evaluarlo y renovarlo, y la recompensa que hace que toda la labor valga la pena.

blocks.en: I. Why Good Plans Fade
blocks.es_reference: I. Por Qué se Desvanecen los Buenos Planes

blocks.en: Good plans rarely fail at their birth; they fail by fading. A plan is launched with enthusiasm, but enthusiasm cools. The founding deacons grow tired or move away; new members and new deacons arrive who never caught the original fire; and slowly, almost without anyone deciding it, the Plan becomes a name on paper that no longer touches lives. The great enemy of the Plan, then, is not usually open opposition but quiet neglect. Nothing dramatic kills it; it simply erodes.
blocks.es_reference: Los buenos planes rara vez fallan en su nacimiento; fallan desvaneciéndose. Un plan se lanza con entusiasmo, pero el entusiasmo se enfría. Los diáconos fundadores se cansan o se mudan; llegan miembros nuevos y diáconos nuevos que nunca captaron el fuego original; y lentamente, casi sin que nadie lo decida, el Plan se convierte en un nombre en el papel que ya no toca vidas. El gran enemigo del Plan, pues, no es usualmente la oposición abierta sino el callado descuido. Nada dramático lo mata; sencillamente se erosiona.

blocks.en: Illustration. A fire that is not tended will go out, however brightly it once burned; a garden left to itself is soon lost to weeds. So it is with this Plan. It must be tended, or it will quietly die. To sustain it is not some optional extra but the very condition of its survival. A church that wants the Plan to last must therefore give thought, from the very beginning, not only to starting it but to keeping it alive.
blocks.es_reference: Ilustración. Un fuego que no se atiza se apagará, por brillante que haya ardido alguna vez; un jardín dejado a sí mismo pronto se pierde entre la maleza. Así es con este Plan. Debe ser atendido, o morirá calladamente. Sostenerlo no es algún extra opcional sino la condición misma de su supervivencia. Una iglesia que quiere que el Plan dure debe, por tanto, dar consideración, desde el mismo comienzo, no solo a empezarlo sino a mantenerlo vivo.

blocks.en: This is no reason for discouragement; it is simply realism. The same is true of every living thing — a marriage, a friendship, a church itself. What is alive must be fed, or it dies. The deacons who understand this from the outset will not be surprised when the Plan needs renewing, but will renew it as a matter of course.
blocks.es_reference: Esto no es razón para el desaliento; es sencillamente realismo. Lo mismo es cierto de toda cosa viva — un matrimonio, una amistad, la iglesia misma. Lo que está vivo debe ser alimentado, o muere. Los diáconos que entienden esto desde el principio no se sorprenderán cuando el Plan necesite renovación, sino que lo renovarán como cosa natural.

blocks.en: II. The Common Challenges
blocks.es_reference: II. Los Desafíos Comunes

blocks.en: Several challenges threaten the Plan over the years, and simply to name them is the first step toward meeting them. The first is neglect and drift, as deacons grow slack and visits grow rare until families are forgotten again. The second is lost vision, as newer deacons and members who never grasped the why come to treat the Plan as mere routine without heart — much like the church that left its first love (Revelation 2:4). The third is overload and burnout, when too many families are laid on too few deacons, and good men wear out and quit. The fourth is untrained deacons, new men set to the work without being taught how, who then do it badly. The fifth is discouragement, for the work is hard, often unseen, and sometimes unthanked, and a deacon can lose heart. The sixth is turnover, as deacons rotate off and pastors change, and the Plan loses its memory and continuity. And the seventh, the deadliest of all, is cold formalism — when the Plan is still carried out, but the love has gone out of it, and it becomes a system instead of a ministry.
blocks.es_reference: Varios desafíos amenazan al Plan a través de los años, y sencillamente nombrarlos es el primer paso para enfrentarlos. El primero es el descuido y la deriva, cuando los diáconos se vuelven flojos y las visitas se vuelven raras hasta que las familias son olvidadas de nuevo. El segundo es la visión perdida, cuando diáconos y miembros más nuevos que nunca captaron el porqué llegan a tratar el Plan como mera rutina sin corazón — muy parecido a la iglesia que dejó su primer amor (Apocalipsis 2:4). El tercero es la sobrecarga y el agotamiento, cuando se ponen demasiadas familias sobre demasiado pocos diáconos, y los hombres buenos se desgastan y renuncian. El cuarto son los diáconos sin entrenar, hombres nuevos puestos a la obra sin que se les enseñe cómo, que luego la hacen mal. El quinto es el desaliento, porque la obra es dura, a menudo invisible, y a veces ingrata, y un diácono puede perder el ánimo. El sexto es la rotación, cuando los diáconos salen y los pastores cambian, y el Plan pierde su memoria y su continuidad. Y el séptimo, el más mortal de todos, es el frío formalismo — cuando el Plan todavía se lleva a cabo, pero el amor se ha ido de él, y se convierte en un sistema en lugar de un ministerio.

blocks.en: Notice that nearly all of these challenges share a single root: they are failures not of structure but of heart and attention. The Plan does not usually collapse because its design was faulty, but because the people running it slowly stopped caring as they once did. That is good news, in a way, for a failure of heart can be repented of and a lapse of attention can be corrected. The remedies, therefore, are less about machinery than about renewal.
blocks.es_reference: Note que casi todos estos desafíos comparten una sola raíz: son fallas no de estructura sino de corazón y de atención. El Plan no suele derrumbarse porque su diseño fuera defectuoso, sino porque las personas que lo dirigen lentamente dejaron de preocuparse como antes lo hacían. Eso es, en cierto modo, buena noticia, porque una falla del corazón puede arrepentirse y un descuido de la atención puede corregirse. Los remedios, por tanto, tienen menos que ver con la maquinaria que con la renovación.

blocks.en: III. Sustaining the Plan: Meeting the Challenges
blocks.es_reference: III. Sosteniendo el Plan: Enfrentando los Desafíos

blocks.en: Against each of these challenges there is a remedy, and a wise church applies them steadily. It must keep casting the vision, teaching and re-teaching the why to every new deacon and to the whole church, again and again; this very course is one such re-casting, and a Plan whose vision is kept fresh will not drift into empty routine. It must train new deacons, passing the work on deliberately, so that new men are taught, mentored, and brought alongside the experienced, and the Plan's skill and heart are handed down. It must keep the loads manageable, enlisting and training more deacons as the church grows and adjusting assignments, so that no deacon is crushed and no family is dropped.
blocks.es_reference: Contra cada uno de estos desafíos hay un remedio, y una iglesia sabia los aplica constantemente. Debe seguir presentando la visión, enseñando y volviendo a enseñar el porqué a cada diácono nuevo y a toda la iglesia, una y otra vez; este mismo curso es una de tales repeticiones, y un Plan cuya visión se mantiene fresca no se desviará hacia la rutina vacía. Debe entrenar a nuevos diáconos, pasando la obra deliberadamente, de modo que los hombres nuevos sean enseñados, guiados, y traídos al lado de los experimentados, y la destreza y el corazón del Plan sean transmitidos. Debe mantener manejables las cargas, reclutando y entrenando a más diáconos conforme la iglesia crece y ajustando las asignaciones, de modo que ningún diácono sea aplastado y ninguna familia sea abandonada.

blocks.en: This passing-on is best done not in a classroom only but shoulder to shoulder. A seasoned deacon who takes a younger man with him on his visits teaches more in a month than a manual could in a year. The new deacon sees how it is done — the gentleness, the listening, the prayer at the bedside — and catches not only the method but the spirit. In this way the heart of the Plan, and not merely its mechanics, passes from one generation of deacons to the next.
blocks.es_reference: Este pasar la obra se hace mejor no solo en un aula sino hombro con hombro. Un diácono experimentado que lleva consigo a un hombre más joven en sus visitas enseña más en un mes que un manual en un año. El nuevo diácono ve cómo se hace — la gentileza, el escuchar, la oración junto a la cama — y capta no solo el método sino el espíritu. De esta manera el corazón del Plan, y no meramente su mecánica, pasa de una generación de diáconos a la siguiente.

blocks.en: It must encourage and refresh the deacons, for the meeting is the place where weary men are strengthened, where fruit is celebrated and burdens shared, and where discouragement is met with brotherly support; “let us not grow weary while doing good, for in due season we shall reap if we do not lose heart” (Galatians 6:9). It must lead the Plan faithfully, the pastor and a faithful head deacon keeping watch that it does not quietly lapse. And it must undergird the whole thing with prayer, for a Plan sustained by human effort alone will fail, while one bathed in prayer and carried by the Spirit of God will endure.
blocks.es_reference: Debe animar y refrescar a los diáconos, porque la reunión es el lugar donde los hombres cansados son fortalecidos, donde el fruto se celebra y las cargas se comparten, y donde el desaliento es enfrentado con apoyo fraternal; «no nos cansemos, pues, de hacer bien; porque a su tiempo segaremos, si no desmayamos» (Gálatas 6:9). Debe dirigir el Plan fielmente, el pastor y un diácono principal fiel velando que no decaiga calladamente. Y debe sostener todo el asunto con oración, porque un Plan sostenido por el esfuerzo humano solo fallará, mientras que uno bañado en oración y llevado por el Espíritu de Dios perdurará.

blocks.en: None of these remedies is complicated, and that is the point. Sustaining the Plan does not call for clever new programs but for the same humble faithfulness that built it — vision kept warm, men kept trained and encouraged, loads kept fair, and the whole thing kept under prayer. A church that simply keeps doing these things will find the Plan still alive and still blessing its people a generation from now.
blocks.es_reference: Ninguno de estos remedios es complicado, y ese es el punto. Sostener el Plan no requiere ingeniosos programas nuevos sino la misma humilde fidelidad que lo edificó — la visión mantenida cálida, los hombres mantenidos entrenados y animados, las cargas mantenidas justas, y todo el asunto mantenido bajo oración. Una iglesia que sencillamente siga haciendo estas cosas hallará el Plan todavía vivo y todavía bendiciendo a su pueblo dentro de una generación.

blocks.en: IV. Evaluating and Renewing the Plan
blocks.es_reference: IV. Evaluando y Renovando el Plan

blocks.en: To sustain the Plan, a church must also evaluate it honestly and regularly, for what is never measured is soon neglected. The Scripture commends exactly this watchfulness over those in our care.
blocks.es_reference: Para sostener el Plan, una iglesia también debe evaluarlo honesta y regularmente, porque lo que nunca se mide pronto se descuida. La Escritura encomienda exactamente esta vigilancia sobre los que están a nuestro cuidado.

blocks.en: Be diligent to know the state of your flocks, and attend to your herds. (Proverbs 27:23, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Sé diligente en conocer el estado de tus ovejas, y mira con cuidado por tus rebaños. (Proverbios 27:23, RVG)

blocks.en: The good shepherd checks the condition of his flock; just so, the church must regularly check the condition of its care.
blocks.es_reference: El buen pastor revisa la condición de su rebaño; justamente así, la iglesia debe revisar regularmente la condición de su cuidado.

blocks.en: Illustration. A man who feels fine may skip his checkups for years; but the doctor who examines him regularly catches the silent trouble while it can still be cured, whereas the man who waits until he feels the pain has often waited too long. A church that never evaluates its Plan is like that man, with the trouble growing unseen until it is advanced. Regular evaluation is the checkup that keeps the Plan healthy.
blocks.es_reference: Ilustración. Un hombre que se siente bien puede saltarse sus chequeos por años; pero el médico que lo examina regularmente atrapa el mal silencioso mientras todavía puede curarse, mientras que el hombre que espera hasta sentir el dolor a menudo ha esperado demasiado. Una iglesia que nunca evalúa su Plan es como ese hombre, con el problema creciendo sin ser visto hasta que está avanzado. La evaluación regular es el chequeo que mantiene sano el Plan.

blocks.en: Such evaluation must be done in honesty but also in grace. Its purpose is never to shame a struggling deacon or to keep a scorecard of failures, but to find the gaps and fill them, so that no family is lost. Handled in that spirit, evaluation is not a threat the deacons dread but a help they welcome — the means by which the whole body keeps its promise that no one will be forgotten.
blocks.es_reference: Tal evaluación debe hacerse con honestidad pero también con gracia. Su propósito nunca es avergonzar a un diácono que batalla ni llevar un marcador de fracasos, sino hallar los vacíos y llenarlos, para que ninguna familia se pierda. Manejada en ese espíritu, la evaluación no es una amenaza que los diáconos temen sino una ayuda que reciben con gusto — el medio por el cual todo el cuerpo guarda su promesa de que nadie será olvidado.

blocks.en: What does a church ask when it evaluates? The honest questions: Is every family still assigned? Is each one actually being contacted and visited? Are real needs being met? Are any deacons overloaded, or any grown slack? Are new members assigned promptly? Are the pastor and deacons still working together well? And by what standard does it measure the answers? Not by activity alone — not merely how many visits were logged — but by fruit: are people actually being loved and cared for? A thick stack of reports is not the goal; cared-for souls are. With the evaluation done, the church renews: assignments are redrawn, deacons are added or retrained, and the whole body recommits. Wise churches make this a regular practice, for an honest yearly review and rededication will keep the Plan from ever drifting far.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Qué pregunta una iglesia cuando evalúa? Las preguntas honestas: ¿Está cada familia todavía asignada? ¿Está cada una siendo de veras contactada y visitada? ¿Se están supliendo las necesidades reales? ¿Hay diáconos sobrecargados, o alguno que se ha vuelto flojo? ¿Se asignan pronto los miembros nuevos? ¿Todavía trabajan bien juntos el pastor y los diáconos? ¿Y por cuál norma mide las respuestas? No por la actividad sola — no meramente cuántas visitas se registraron — sino por el fruto: ¿está la gente siendo de veras amada y cuidada? Un grueso montón de informes no es la meta; las almas cuidadas lo son. Hecha la evaluación, la iglesia renueva: las asignaciones se vuelven a trazar, se añaden o se vuelven a entrenar diáconos, y todo el cuerpo se vuelve a comprometer. Las iglesias sabias hacen de esto una práctica regular, porque una honesta revisión y rededicación anual evitará que el Plan se desvíe jamás muy lejos.

blocks.en: V. The Reward of Faithfulness
blocks.es_reference: V. La Recompensa de la Fidelidad

blocks.en: All of this — the sustaining, the evaluating, the pressing on — asks much of a church and of its deacons. Is it worth it? It is, beyond all measure. It is worth it, first, because souls are worth it. Every family kept from slipping away, every burden carried, every soul won and discipled, is of infinite worth to God; and the Plan is, in the end, simply the love of Christ organized so that none of His people is forgotten. And it is worth it, second, because the labor is not in vain, for the deacon labors not for the praise of men but for the eye of his Master.
blocks.es_reference: Todo esto — el sostener, el evaluar, el seguir adelante — pide mucho de una iglesia y de sus diáconos. ¿Vale la pena? Lo vale, más allá de toda medida. Lo vale, primero, porque las almas lo valen. Cada familia guardada de perderse, cada carga llevada, cada alma ganada y discipulada, es de infinito valor para Dios; y el Plan es, al final, sencillamente el amor de Cristo organizado para que ninguno de su pueblo sea olvidado. Y lo vale, segundo, porque la labor no es en vano, porque el diácono labora no por la alabanza de los hombres sino para el ojo de su Maestro.

blocks.en: And the fruit of such faithfulness reaches further than any deacon will see in his lifetime. The lonely widow who was visited, the wandering young man who was sought, the family that was carried through its darkest week — these are touched in ways that ripple on for generations, into children and grandchildren who grew up knowing that the church loved them. A deacon plants trees under whose shade he may never sit; but they grow, and they bless, long after he is gone.
blocks.es_reference: Y el fruto de tal fidelidad alcanza más lejos de lo que ningún diácono verá en su vida. La viuda solitaria que fue visitada, el joven errante que fue buscado, la familia que fue llevada a través de su semana más oscura — estos son tocados de maneras que se extienden por generaciones, hacia hijos y nietos que crecieron sabiendo que la iglesia los amaba. Un diácono planta árboles bajo cuya sombra quizá nunca se siente; pero crecen, y bendicen, mucho después de que él se ha ido.

blocks.en: Well done, good and faithful servant; you were faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord. (Matthew 25:21, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Bien, buen siervo y fiel; sobre poco has sido fiel, sobre mucho te pondré; entra en el gozo de tu señor. (Mateo 25:21, RVG)

blocks.en: This is the word that every faithful deacon longs one day to hear. He may labor here unseen and unthanked, but he labors for his Master, and when the Chief Shepherd appears he will receive the crown of glory that does not fade away (1 Peter 5:4). Let no deacon, then, grow weary. The work is hard, but it is holy; it is often hidden, but it is never wasted; and its reward, in the joy of the Lord, is sure.
blocks.es_reference: Esta es la palabra que todo diácono fiel anhela un día oír. Puede laborar aquí sin ser visto y sin ser agradecido, pero labora para su Maestro, y cuando aparezca el Príncipe de los pastores recibirá la corona incorruptible de gloria (1 Pedro 5:4). Que ningún diácono, pues, se canse. La obra es dura, pero es santa; es a menudo escondida, pero nunca es desperdiciada; y su recompensa, en el gozo del Señor, es segura.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión

blocks.en: We have reached the end of our journey together. We have seen what a deacon is and what he must be; we have traced the vision, the definition, and the building of the Plan; we have followed the deacon into homes and hospitals, into discipleship and evangelism, into crisis and confidence; we have watched the deacons gather and uphold their pastor; and we have learned, at the last, how to keep it all alive. Yet all of it comes down to one thing. The Deacon Family Ministry Plan is not, finally, a program or a system. It is love — the love of Christ, who came not to be served but to serve, carried through His servants into every family of His church, so that no one is forgotten and no one is left alone.
blocks.es_reference: Hemos llegado al final de nuestro camino juntos. Hemos visto qué es un diácono y qué debe ser; hemos trazado la visión, la definición, y la construcción del Plan; hemos seguido al diácono a los hogares y los hospitales, al discipulado y el evangelismo, a la crisis y la confianza; hemos observado a los diáconos reunirse y sostener a su pastor; y hemos aprendido, al fin, cómo mantenerlo todo vivo. Sin embargo, todo se reduce a una sola cosa. El Plan de Ministerio Familiar del Diácono no es, finalmente, un programa ni un sistema. Es amor — el amor de Cristo, que no vino para ser servido sino para servir, llevado por medio de sus siervos a cada familia de su iglesia, para que nadie sea olvidado y nadie quede solo.

blocks.en: If you are a deacon, or one day will be, let this be your aim: not to fill an office, but to love a people; not to hold a title, but to wash feet; not merely to run a plan, but to be, to a handful of families, the very hands of Christ. Do that, faithfully and to the end, and you will have done something that will outlast every building and budget — you will have loved as your Lord loved.
blocks.es_reference: Si usted es un diácono, o un día lo será, sea este su propósito: no llenar un oficio, sino amar a un pueblo; no ostentar un título, sino lavar pies; no meramente operar un plan, sino ser, para un puñado de familias, las manos mismas de Cristo. Haga eso, fielmente y hasta el fin, y habrá hecho algo que sobrevivirá a todo edificio y presupuesto — habrá amado como su Señor amó.

blocks.en: “Therefore, my beloved brethren, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.” May God raise up faithful deacons who will take up this towel, this Plan, this love, and carry it well — until the Chief Shepherd comes.
blocks.es_reference: «Así que, hermanos míos amados, estad firmes y constantes, creciendo en la obra del Señor siempre, sabiendo que vuestro trabajo en el Señor no es en vano.» Que Dios levante diáconos fieles que tomen esta toalla, este Plan, este amor, y lo lleven bien — hasta que venga el Príncipe de los pastores.

blocks.es_reference: Examen Final de la Unidad 10

blocks.es_reference: Certificado: las 20 preguntas de opción múltiple. Asociado: opción múltiple y las 10 preguntas de completar el espacio en blanco. Si no aprueba, el examen espera un tiempo breve antes de intentarlo de nuevo.

fill.prompt: The great enemy of the Plan is not usually open opposition but quiet ____: nobody decides to kill it, people simply stop looking after it until it erodes.
Lost vision can make the Plan mere routine without heart, much like the church that left its first ____ (Revelation 2:4).
The deadliest challenge of all is cold ____, when the Plan is still carried out but the love has gone out of it.

"Be diligent to know the state of your ____, and attend to your herds" (Proverbs 27:23).

sa.prompt: Why do good plans usually fail, and what does this mean for sustaining the Plan?
sa.model: Good plans usually fail not at their birth but by slowly fading. A plan is launched with enthusiasm, but the enthusiasm cools, the founding deacons tire or move away, new members arrive who never caught the original fire, and the Plan becomes a name on paper that no longer touches lives. The great enemy is therefore not open opposition but quiet neglect. This means that sustaining the Plan is not optional maintenance but the very condition of its survival. Like a fire that must be tended or a garden that must be weeded, the Plan must be deliberately kept alive, or it will quietly die.

sa.prompt: What are the common challenges that threaten the Plan over the years?
sa.model: Several challenges threaten the Plan over the years. There is neglect and drift, as deacons grow slack and families are forgotten again. There is lost vision, as newer deacons treat the Plan as mere routine without heart. There is overload and burnout, when too many families are laid on too few deacons. There is the problem of untrained deacons who do the work badly. There is discouragement, since the work is hard and often unthanked. There is turnover, as deacons rotate off and pastors change. And the deadliest of all is cold formalism, when the Plan is still carried out but the love has gone out of it and it becomes a system instead of a ministry.

sa.prompt: How does a church sustain the Plan and meet its challenges?
sa.model: A church sustains the Plan by applying steady remedies to each challenge. It keeps casting the vision, teaching and re-teaching the why to every new deacon and to the whole church. It trains new deacons deliberately, best of all shoulder to shoulder, so the heart and not just the method is handed down. It keeps the loads manageable, enlisting more deacons as the church grows. It encourages and refreshes the deacons in the meeting, so the weary do not lose heart. It leads the Plan faithfully through the pastor and a head deacon, and it undergirds the whole thing with prayer. None of these remedies is complicated; they are simply the same humble faithfulness that built the Plan.

sa.prompt: Why and how must a church evaluate the Plan?
sa.model: A church must evaluate the Plan because what is never measured is soon neglected. Scripture commands this watchfulness, telling us to be diligent to know the state of our flocks; the good shepherd checks his flock, and the church must check its care. Like a regular medical checkup that catches silent trouble early, evaluation finds problems before they grow advanced. In evaluating, the church asks honest questions: is every family still assigned, contacted, and visited; are real needs being met; are any deacons overloaded or slack; are new members assigned promptly; do the pastor and deacons still work well together. Then it renews, redrawing assignments and recommitting.

sa.prompt: By what standard should the Plan be measured, and in what spirit should evaluation be done?
sa.model: The Plan should be measured not by activity alone, such as how many visits were logged, but by fruit: whether people are actually being loved and cared for. A thick stack of reports is not the goal; cared-for souls are. The real test is whether the love is reaching the people. And the evaluation must be done in honesty but also in grace. Its purpose is never to shame a struggling deacon or to keep a scorecard of failures, but to find the gaps and fill them, so that no family is lost. Handled in that spirit, evaluation is not a threat the deacons dread but a help they welcome.

sa.prompt: Why is the labor of the Plan worth it, even when it is hard?
sa.model: The labor of the Plan is worth it beyond all measure, for two reasons. First, because souls are worth it. Every family kept from slipping away, every burden carried, every soul won and discipled, is of infinite worth to God, and the Plan is finally just the love of Christ organized so that none of His people is forgotten. Second, because the labor is not in vain. The deacon labors not for the praise of men but for the eye of his Master, who has promised that our labor in the Lord is never in vain. So the deacon should not grow weary, for the work is hard but holy, often hidden but never wasted.

sa.prompt: What reward does the faithful deacon have, according to Matthew 25:21 and 1 Peter 5:4?
sa.model: According to Matthew 25:21, the faithful deacon's reward is to hear his Master say, Well done, good and faithful servant; you were faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things, enter into the joy of your lord. This is the word every faithful deacon longs one day to hear. And according to 1 Peter 5:4, when the Chief Shepherd appears, he will receive the crown of glory that does not fade away. He may labor here unseen and unthanked, but he labors for his Master and not for the praise of men, and his reward in the joy of the Lord is sure.

sa.prompt: How far does the fruit of a deacon's faithfulness reach?
sa.model: The fruit of a deacon's faithfulness reaches far further than he will ever see in his own lifetime. The lonely widow who was visited, the wandering young man who was sought, the family that was carried through its darkest week, are touched in ways that ripple on for generations, into children and grandchildren who grow up knowing that the church loved them. In this way a deacon plants trees under whose shade he may never sit, but which grow and bless long after he is gone. His hidden, faithful labor outlasts him, because love, once given in Christ's name, never truly dies.

sa.prompt: What is the Deacon Family Ministry Plan, finally, when all is said?
sa.model: When all is said, the Deacon Family Ministry Plan is not finally a program or a system. It is love. It is the love of Christ, who came not to be served but to serve and to give His life a ransom for many, carried through His servants into every family of His church, so that no one is forgotten and no one is left alone. All the structure, the assigning, the visiting, the reporting, exists only to serve that love, and the love exists only to carry Christ Himself to His people. The Plan is simply a way of making sure that the love which the church professes actually reaches every single soul.

sa.prompt: Summarize how the Plan is to be sustained through the years.
sa.model: The Plan is sustained through the years by honest, steady faithfulness. A church faces the challenges that erode it, such as neglect, lost vision, overload, and cold formalism, and it meets them by keeping the vision warm, training new deacons, keeping loads manageable, encouraging the deacons, leading faithfully, and undergirding all with prayer. It evaluates the Plan regularly and honestly, measuring by fruit rather than mere activity, and renews it as needed. And it presses on in the assurance that the labor is not in vain, that souls are worth it, and that the faithful deacon will one day hear his Master say, Well done. So sustained, the Plan keeps the love of Christ reaching every family for generations.
